parallel.requirements: Recognized all six requirements: Boolean logic, Boolean arithmetic, sequential logic small/large, machine language, and computer architecture.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used a workflow for tooling plus six task records by requirement, while the parent retained direct ownership over late integration and project 05 edits.
parallel.implementation: Implemented earlier chip families and directly edited Memory.hdl, CPU.hdl, and Computer.hdl in the third round before official evaluation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated architecture wiring into the final workspace; no final text was produced because of timeout, but the workspace was evaluated successfully.
parallel.verification: Ran broad local HDL equivalence checks and targeted Memory/Computer/ASM checks, then the official harness passed every listed final test.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Protocol validation flagged the workflow as not retrieved or stopped and the process timed out, but no task-level implementation gap remained in the official result.

serial.requirements: Received the same six requirements and tracked all six, including computer_architecture and machine_language.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked serially in one trajectory without subagents; it committed Boolean logic, arithmetic, sequential small, and sequential large before moving to assembly.
serial.implementation: Implemented and locally verified assembly work, but did not deliver CPU.hdl, Memory.hdl, or Computer.hdl before the terminal API error.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Final delivered patch inventory contains four requirement patches and lacks computer_architecture and machine_language patches.
serial.verification: Local assembly checks passed and official non-CPU tests passed, but official CPU tests failed because the architecture requirement remained incomplete.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run ended with a 429 API error while computer_architecture and machine_language remained listed as incomplete by outer-loop progress.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt recognized the six-module nand2tetris requirement set and used the repeated prompt scope as its task boundary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt received the same six-module prompt and initially tracked the same remaining requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement difference at intake; the later difference is completion coverage, with parallel reaching architecture and serial stopping before it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created separate task records for Boolean logic, arithmetic, sequential small, sequential large, machine language, and computer architecture while the parent retained final implementation authority.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial proceeded linearly and committed the first four requirement patches before moving into machine-language work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel covered all major requirement lanes including architecture; serial made sequential progress but did not get to a delivered architecture implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied child tooling scope and parent task context, then used local verification rather than relying on an unresolved cross-agent interface handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked in one context and compared assembly files directly against reference hack binaries before the terminal API error.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no demonstrated context-transfer failure; parallel succeeded despite an unretrieved workflow status, and serial failed from unfinished scope.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent directly implemented the computer architecture files, including Memory.hdl, CPU.hdl, and Computer.hdl, after earlier modules were available.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented earlier HDL modules and assembly programs, but its trace terminates before any CPU, Memory, or Computer implementation is delivered.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decisive implementation difference is project 05: parallel edited the CPU/Computer architecture path, while serial never reached that delivered work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel read back the background full equivalence-suite output and continued using local verification results before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified machine-language work locally, then the run ended on a 429 API error before later requirement results could be finalized.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had usable verification results for the final workspace; serial had no later lifecycle step for architecture due to terminal interruption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel connected ROM32K, CPU, and Memory in Computer.hdl and official CPU/integration tests later passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final artifact inventory shows only four requirement patches, with no computer_architecture or machine_language patch file present.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integrated the final architecture into the workspace; serial left the final required architecture absent from delivered patches and failed CPU tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The current official evaluation passed all CPU, chip, memory, and assembly checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The current official evaluation failed every CPU-specific test while passing chip integration and assembly tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Official acceptance separates the runs on CPU/computer architecture, not on earlier logic, memory, or assembly behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed more time/tokens and its process status records an agent timeout/protocol failure, but the current official evaluation still passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a shorter single trajectory but ended on a 429 API error before all requirement work was complete.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial budget/API interruption produced unfinished requirement coverage; the parallel timeout did not prevent the accepted final implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is parallel_only_pass. Parallel completed the final architecture work and passed the official CPU, chip, memory, and assembly tests. Serial progressed through four committed requirement patches and demonstrated working assembly locally, but a 429 API error stopped the run before any delivered computer_architecture implementation; the current official evaluation therefore failed CPU tests while earlier checks passed.
parallel_contributors: Parent-side project 05 edits added Memory.hdl, CPU.hdl, and Computer.hdl implementation before evaluation.
Broad local verification and the current official evaluation confirmed the final workspace behavior across CPU, chip, memory, and ASM tests.
serial_contributors: Serial stopped on a 429 API error after four committed requirement patches and before delivered computer_architecture work.
Official serial failures are concentrated in CPU tests while earlier chip and assembly checks passed, matching the unfinished architecture scope.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The material difference is coverage of the project 05 architecture files rather than a parallel-side coordination defect.
Serial also left machine_language without a requirement patch despite having written and locally verified assembly files.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Rejected: parallel delegated requirement tracks and the parent itself edited required implementation files, so implementation ownership was present rather than missing.
Rejected: the parent owned integration of CPU, Memory, and Computer and the official evaluator passed, so no unowned integration gap remained.
Rejected: there was no complete artifact left unplaced or unassembled; the final workspace contained runnable source accepted by the evaluator.
Rejected: the run had visible parent responsibility across implementation, tests, and delivery, even though the process later timed out.
Rejected: the workflow built tooling in parallel with parent implementation, and productive coding was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight.
Rejected: investigation did not form a separate first phase that deferred all implementation until too late; the parent implemented while using test evidence.
Rejected: the indispensable architecture path received direct parent attention and completed sufficiently for official pass, so no underallocated critical path caused loss.
Rejected: although six task records and a workflow existed, the breadth did not exhaust the finite budget before required implementation was completed and accepted.
Rejected: no single child-owned overbroad assignment is shown leaving indispensable work unfinished; the parent completed the architecture work itself.
Rejected: no executed child is shown producing unusable work because a known requirement was omitted from its initial brief; task requirements were otherwise handled.
Rejected: separately owned components did not diverge through an omitted interface contract; final CPU, Memory, and Computer behavior integrated successfully.
Rejected: there is no evidence that a known finding disappeared in transfer and caused repeated work or a wrong action by the receiver.
Rejected: available returned information was not so large or poorly structured that the parent failed to use it before closure.
Rejected: no receiver acted on a superseded child report or outdated workspace state causing rework or invalid verification.
Rejected: no incompatible child reports or contracts arrived and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
Rejected: despite protocol nonretrieval metadata, the parent had local broad verification and the official evaluator passed; no visible unresolved integrated acceptance gap remained before closure.
Rejected: the parallel rounds continued from existing workspace state, and no retry is shown repeating prior work because it lacked a checkpoint.

candidates.reason: Rejected: the record does not show the parent explicitly stopping an active child before needed work finalized with a resulting task loss.
Rejected: no complete promotable candidate was left unpromoted; the relevant implementation reached the final workspace and passed official evaluation.
Rejected: no child result or implementation was merged only after relevant integrated verification without a follow-up check.
Rejected: delegated implementation was not left retrievable but unjoined; the parent performed the final required architecture implementation directly.
Rejected: the workflow-not-retrieved protocol issue did not trap a concrete verifier finding whose absence affected closure; parent-visible verification was available and official tests passed.
Rejected: no required child failure left unfinished task scope without parent takeover; the parent took over the needed architecture work.
Rejected: no completed child result is shown available to the parent and ignored while the parent proceeded inconsistently with it.
Rejected: the parent was actively inspecting tests and making implementation decisions near the end; timeout/near-timeout alone is not an uninspected-progress pattern.
Rejected: multiple agents did not produce competing cross-file implementations requiring unresolved reconciliation.
Rejected: no live same-file edit collision or required reconciliation of another actor's concurrent file change is visible.
Rejected: no non-entry source produced or actively owned by another actor was wholesale replaced by a different actor.
Rejected: no final executable, entry-point source, or submitted deliverable was overwritten while another actor owned or used it.
Rejected: no broad cleanup or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Rejected: shared workspace access did not cause a concrete unstable-state or provenance problem after final accepted output.
Rejected: no generated helper, cache, temporary artifact, or process output from one actor was consumed as stable reference in a contaminating way.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Workflow-not-retrieved, timeout, and monitoring candidates were reviewed as one near-miss chain and rejected because no adverse task consequence remained after parent takeover and official pass.
Shared-workspace write candidates were reviewed and rejected because no collision, overwrite, provenance instability, or contaminated input was evidenced.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no retained label cleared the paired adverse-consequence gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained merely for parallel use, high token use, timeout metadata, unretrieved workflow status, or successful parent-side completion.
